translation: Target is the proposition that for every set T of arithmetic sentences (not required to be closed under deduction) equipped with a Δ₁ arithmetical definition of its axiom set, if every sentence in T is true in the standard model of arithmetic (the natural numbers), then the theory consisting of T together with the set of all local reflection sentences Prov_T(⌜σ⌝) → σ (one for every arithmetic sentence σ, where Prov_T is the standard provability predicate built from T's Δ₁ presentation) is consistent (does not derive a contradiction in classical first-order logic). No further strength assumption on T (such as containing IΣ₁) is required.

divergences.description: Conclusion weakened from soundness to consistency: Chalmers's parenthetical explicitly states that supplementing a sound system with a true statement 'yields a sound system' (and the main text concludes that F' is sound), whereas Target only concludes Entailment.Consistent (T ∪ T.localReflectionOn Set.univ). Consistency is strictly weaker than soundness, even though soundness (Def3) is already defined in the context.

Arbitrary true statement (and 'I am F') replaced by T's local reflection schema: Chalmers's parenthetical states a general principle for supplementing a sound system with any true statement, and the main text applies it specifically to the assumption 'I am F'. Target does not quantify over arbitrary true statements and instead supplements T only with T.localReflectionOn Set.univ (the sentences Prov_T(⌜σ⌝) → σ expressing T's soundness), which neither captures the general principle of the parenthetical nor represents the assumption 'I am F' added to F in the passage.

Omission of epistemic and indexical content: The surrounding sentences in the passage are framed epistemically ('I know that I am F', 'I know that F is sound', 'I know that F' is sound') and rely on indexical self-reference ('I am F', 'I am sound'), none of which can be expressed in first-order arithmetic (ℒₒᵣ). This is minor relative to the author's claim because the parenthetical itself is non-epistemic.

Restriction to Δ₁-presented first-order arithmetic theories: The passage speaks generally of a 'sound system', whereas Target restricts T to a set of sentences in first-order arithmetic (ArithmeticTheory) equipped with a Δ₁ arithmetical presentation of its axioms ([T.Δ₁]). The Δ₁ hypothesis is unnecessary for Chalmers's parenthetical itself and is only required to construct Prov_T for the local reflection schema.

Infinite schema vs. single statement: The parenthetical speaks of adding a single 'true statement', whereas Target adds the infinite set T.localReflectionOn Set.univ, reflecting the fact that first-order arithmetic cannot express soundness as a single sentence.

judgement.summary: Target diverges materially from Chalmers's parenthetical in two major ways: it weakens the conclusion from soundness ('yields a sound system') to mere consistency, and it replaces the general claim about adding any true statement (applied in the passage to 'I am F') with the specific case of adding T's local reflection schema. It also restricts to Δ₁-presented arithmetic theories and omits the surrounding passage's epistemic and indexical framing.
